steps: Resuscitate; correct hypokalaemia and hypoglycaemia (cerebral glucose may be low despite normal serum).
Activated charcoal if early; generous IV fluids.
Urinary alkalinisation with IV sodium bicarbonate (target urine pH ~7.5–8) — enhances elimination; keep K replete.
HAEMODIALYSIS for severe toxicity (high levels, acidosis, CNS features, renal failure, pulmonary oedema).
Avoid intubation if possible (loss of compensatory hyperventilation is dangerous); serial levels.

drugRefs.dose: 1 mmol/kg IV bolus (8.4%), then infusion (e.g. 1.26% / 1.4%) titrated to urine pH 7.5–8
drugRefs.freq: continuous infusion, titrated to urine pH
drugRefs.why: Alkalinises urine to trap ionised salicylate and enhance renal elimination; also corrects acidaemia which otherwise increases CNS salicylate entry. Requires concurrent potassium repletion to be effective.

drugRefs.freq: single dose if within ~1 hour (consider repeat doses for large ingestions)
drugRefs.why: Adsorbs unabsorbed salicylate; most useful early and for the modified-release/concretion-forming ingestions typical of salicylates.

drugRefs.dose: add per serum K⁺ (e.g. 40 mmol/L in IV fluids)
drugRefs.why: Hypokalaemia prevents effective urinary alkalinisation (kidney exchanges K⁺ for H⁺); keep potassium replete throughout.

drugRefs.freq: for hypoglycaemia or altered mental status
drugRefs.why: CNS glucose may be low despite normal serum glucose; give to any patient with neurological features.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Poisoning and Drug Overdose (Salicylates)
EXTRIP Workgroup Recommendations — Extracorporeal Treatment for Salicylate Poisoning

confirm: Tinnitus, hyperventilation, nausea, agitation with a mixed respiratory alkalosis + high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis; rising salicylate level.
